claims.text: Rapid thermal-shock processing of equimolar Pd–Pt–Rh–Ir–Ru precursors yields near-atomic-level elemental homogeneity in 5–15 nm nanoparticles.
Elemental homogeneity creates a continuous distribution of active surface ensembles.
The resulting surface ensembles optimally tune the distribution of d-band centers.
The tuned d-band-center distribution lowers the ORR activation barrier.
Rapid thermal-shock processing enhances ORR activity relative to conventional slow annealing.
Rapid thermal shock locks the five noble metals into a single-phase FCC lattice.
Uniform mixing in the FCC lattice produces a spectrum of surface atomic ensembles.
The spectrum of surface ensembles shifts and broadens the HEA d-band-center distribution.
The altered d-band-center distribution decreases the energy barrier for O–O bond cleavage during ORR.
The rapid-thermal-shock sample will have per-element composition variance below 5 at.%.
The rapid-thermal-shock sample will have 20–30% higher ORR kinetic current density at 0.9 V versus RHE than the slow-annealed sample.
The slow-annealed baseline will exhibit per-element composition variance above 10 at.%.
The slow-annealed baseline will exhibit lower ORR activity than the rapid-thermal-shock sample.

The proposed relationship should hold for equimolar Pd–Pt–Rh–Ir–Ru HEAs with particle sizes of 5–15 nm, processing temperatures of 600–1200 °C, inert atmosphere, carbon support, and acidic ORR testing at 25 °C.
